key_insight: WorldCompass is an RL post-training framework that steers autoregressive, video-based world models by using interaction signals to explore and prefer accurate, consistent long-horizon continuations via targeted clip-level rollouts.
problem_solved: Video world models degrade over long horizons because autoregressive sampling compounds errors and lacks a mechanism to use interaction feedback; WorldCompass addresses how to explore and select long-horizon trajectories that remain accurate and coherent.
method: Clip-level rollout strategy: generate multiple candidate continuations for a single target clip, evaluate them, and use those evaluations to guide longer rollouts.

RL-based post-training policy: frame sample selection/steering as a reinforcement learning problem using interaction-derived rewards (accuracy, consistency) to update a steering policy without retraining the base video model.
Long-horizon aggregation: compose clip-level decisions into coherent long-horizon trajectories and optimize the steering objective to reduce drift and improve consistency over many steps.
impact: Provides a practical way to make autoregressive video world models more reliable for long-horizon simulation, improving downstream planning, model-based RL, and any application that needs consistent multi-step visual predictions.
visual_elements: Diagram of clip-level rollouts: one input clip branching into multiple candidate continuations with scores and a selected path.
Before vs after long-horizon trajectories: side-by-side timelines showing drift/error accumulation vs stabilized predictions.
RL feedback loop: interaction signals → reward computation → steering policy → sampling decisions (post-training layer).
Bar/line chart: prediction error or task performance as a function of horizon (short → long) comparing baseline and WorldCompass.
paper_title: WorldCompass: Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon World Models
paper_authors: Zehan Wang, Tengfei Wang, Haiyu Zhang, Xuhui Zuo, Junta Wu
